data.current_summary: Step 1 of the compliant upload: get a presigned PUT for the user's video FILE
data.current_description: Everpop clips from the creator's file, never from a YouTube download. PUT exactly expectedBytes to the returned putUrl (15-min validity, ≤5 GB — the most one PUT can carry, files up to 32 GB go through browserUploadUrl — .mp4/.mov/.webm/.mkv/.m4v), send every requiredHeaders entry, and let the HTTP client supply Content-Length. Then call /api/v1/videos/complete. If the PUT times out or the connection drops, or a retried PUT answers 412 (If-None-Match: * means the bytes are already stored), call /api/v1/videos/complete with the same key before anything else: a 400 there means the bytes never landed (PUT again while putUrl is valid, else cancel the slot). At most 3 uploads can be open at once (429 upload_slots).
data.summary_suggestion: Request presigned upload slot for video file
data.description_suggestion: Initiates a direct file upload by returning a presigned PUT URL and upload slot. Supports video files up to 5 GB per PUT request (files up to 32 GB use browserUploadUrl). Supported formats: .mp4, .mov, .webm, .mkv, .m4v. The PUT URL is valid for 15 minutes. You must PUT exactly expectedBytes, include all requiredHeaders, and let the HTTP client supply Content-Length. After uploading, call POST /api/v1/videos/complete with the same key to finalize. If the PUT times out, drops, or returns 412, call /api/v1/videos/complete first to check status (400 means bytes never landed; retry the PUT if still valid, or cancel the slot). Maximum 3 concurrent upload slots per user (returns 429 if exceeded). Everpop only clips from creator-owned files, not YouTube downloads.
